segments.text: Taking a phone picture is easy. Open the app, point, and tap.
For most pictures, that's all you need.
But if it's dark outside, you turn on the flash.
Or sitting high in the stands,
wanting a clear picture of a hockey player, you zoom in.
You don't change these settings for every single picture.
But knowing when to use them helps you get exactly the picture you want.
AI works much the same way.
Depending on the app and your subscription, you may have three other choices.
The model, thinking, and research.
You won't need to change them every time.
But knowing what they do helps you get a better answer.
When you use an AI app, a large language model, or LLM, powers its answers.
Think of the LLM as the engine inside the app.
When an app lets you choose a model,
you're choosing which specific LLM to use.
Different models have different capabilities.
And knowing which one to choose helps you get better answers.
This board lays out the first choice.
Which model?
Let's look at the options.
On the left, the everyday model is for quick questions and simple tasks.
For example, you would ask,
suggest a funny movie to watch tonight.
On the right, the more capable model is for more demanding tasks with details to work through.
For example, ask,
Help me plan a summer business, including costs, pricing, and how many customers I'll need.
The rule at the bottom provides a clear baseline.
Start with the default, try a more capable model when needed.
Selecting the right model ensures the AI has the adequate horsepower
for the specific complexity of your prompt.
Choosing a model changes which LLM you use.
Thinking changes how much time AI spends working through your task.
Think about it like this.
For your first English exam,
you have to write an essay about the book you read over the summer.
Before you start writing, you decide what you want to say,
which examples support your points, and how to organize them.
Thinking mode serves a similar purpose.
AI isn't thinking the way you do,
but it spends more time working through the task before giving you an answer.
This next board asks, how much thinking?
With less thinking, AI spends less time working through your task.
It is useful for less complicated and routine work.
For example, ask,
turn these notes from our group meeting into a clear checklist.
With more thinking, AI spends more time working through steps,
weighing options and checking its answer.
It is useful for tasks that require analysis,
like coding, planning, and problems with steps.
For example, ask, help us divide this project among four people.
We have one week, different schedules,
and only two people know how to edit video.
Check the bottom banner.
Give AI more time when the task needs more working through.
Thinking mode doesn't change the engine itself.
It simply gives the engine permission to process the problem
in multiple deliberate steps before returning an answer.
There's one more option to consider.
Research.
Stop at an in-and-out for a cheeseburger
and you know enough to place your order.
Buying your first house is different.
You'd want to compare prices,
learn about the neighborhoods,
and check how far each house is from work.
It's a bigger decision,
and you need more information before making it.
AI's research mode helps with that kind of work.
It gathers information from different websites
and brings it together so you can compare your options.
Regular chat can look things up too.
Research is useful when you want a fuller investigation
across several sources.
This final board asks, how much research?
Use regular chat to simply get an answer to a question.
For example, ask, I live in Dallas.
How long would it take me to drive to Texas A&M
and college station versus UT Austin?
Use deep research to get information from many websites,
compare what they say,
and build a report that shows sources.
For example, ask, I want to study physics
and I'm considering Texas A&M and UT Austin.
Compare their physics programs,
undergraduate research opportunities,
admissions requirements, and costs.
Show your sources.
The rule across the bottom is clear.
Use deeper research when you need to compare information
across sources.
Research mode elevates the AI from a simple lookup tool
into an active investigator,
capable of comparing complex real-world options.
Model, thinking, research.
Use them when the work demands more.
